Chapter 7: Missions and the Spread of Joy
You know that feeling when you hear stories from faraway places—tales about people you’ve never met, living lives so different from your own? There’s a restlessness that stirs inside, isn’t there? The world feels huge, and sometimes, the needs out there can seem almost too much to even think about.
For a lot of folks, the idea of missions—of actually going somewhere new to serve—can feel like it’s only for the really brave or the truly selfless. Maybe it seems like something you’d only do if you were ready to leave everything comfortable behind. Honestly, it can sound a bit overwhelming.
But let’s take a step back and picture something different. Imagine a group of friends gathered around a table, swapping stories about moments that changed them. There’s laughter, maybe a few tears, and a sense of amazement at what God is doing in places you might not even find on a map. The energy in the room isn’t coming from guilt or pressure—it’s from a deep, shared joy. The kind of joy that makes you want others to experience it too.
That’s when you start to see missions in a whole new light. It’s not about duty or checking off a list. It’s about joy overflowing. When you find real satisfaction in God, it just makes sense to want others to have that same experience. Going, serving, stepping out of your comfort zone—it isn’t a burden anymore. It’s actually a privilege. Almost like being invited to join in the spread of something beautiful: God’s glory, and the fullness of joy that comes with it.
Let me tell you about a young person who once heard about needs in a distant country. At first, there was fear. Fear of not knowing what to expect, fear of leaving comfort behind, fear of messing up. But the more they thought about the joy they’d already found in God, the less the fear mattered. That desire to share joy, to see it ripple out beyond their own life, just grew and grew. Choosing to go wasn’t easy—it never is—but instead of dread, there was this growing sense of anticipation. Like, what could happen if I say yes?
Here’s something to pay attention to: missions isn’t really about convincing people to accept a set of rules or beliefs. At its heart, it’s about inviting them into a relationship with the source of all joy. The message isn’t “you have to”—it’s “you get to.” The more you experience God’s joy, the more you want to see it reach every corner of the world.
And this way of seeing things totally changes how you think about sacrifices. Sure, there are challenges—being far from home, facing discomfort, not always being understood. But those things don’t weigh as much when you’re watching lives be transformed right in front of you. The cost doesn’t go away, but it feels different. When you’re chasing after joy in God, even the hardest sacrifices start to seem worthwhile.
So, here’s the key takeaway: missions isn’t just about going somewhere else. It’s about the unstoppable spread of joy—joy that’s too good to keep to yourself.
